$comment: Invariant ids the P2 round-3 task `p2r3/expand-bake-package` turns green in tools/coursekit (G7 expand, G8 bake, G9 package). `owned` IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and the reason is NOT that the gate cannot see these tests: scripts/coverage-map.ts reads both pytest claim forms (the snake id in the `def` name and the bracketed ids leading a test's own docstring), `TEST_ROOTS` includes `tools`, and `pnpm test:coverage-map` prints OK for all eight ids from this lane's tests. The reason is COLLISION. Coverage-map fails when two ownership files claim the same id, and all eight are already claimed by earlier files: docs/owned/p2-g7.json owns INV-PACK-07 and INV-PACK-50 (with INV-PACK-08), p2-g8.json owns INV-PACK-15 and INV-AUD-08, p2-g9.json owns INV-PACK-17 and INV-PACK-41, p2-g1-g2.json owns INV-PACK-51 (with INV-PACK-40), and docs/owned/packs.json owns INV-PACK-02. So this lane RE-GREENS ids it does not own, and claiming them here would turn `test:coverage-map` red on a duplicate rather than add coverage. Two different relationships hide under that: for the six P2 ids the earlier lane declared the id AND wrote the test, and this lane is what makes that test run over a course that exists; for INV-PACK-02 the claim sits in a P1 TypeScript lane's file (docs/owned/packs.json) and the first PYTEST test carrying the id is new here. `owningTests` says which is which per id. (A previous version of this comment said coverage-map could not read pytest and that p2-g7/p2-g8/p2-g9 carried `owned: []`. Both were false; only p2-deps-scaffold.json is empty. Corrected here because a false reason in an ownership file is what makes the next lane re-derive it.) `ownedByPytest` and `owningTests` below are the record of which test in this lane greens which id.

rulings.B14 — a starved slot: `StageResult(ok=False)`, message verbatim. Implemented as `StarvedSlot(LookupError)` raised by `_resolve` and caught in `expand`, with EVERY PASS now inside the stage's `try` — pass 1 (resolve + align) was outside it, which is why the one content failure most likely on a real course printed a Python traceback where every other stage prints a line and exits 4. `LookupError` rather than `KeyError` because `KeyError.__str__` renders the repr of its argument and wraps the sentence in quotes. Pinned by test_B14_a_starved_gap_slot_is_a_stage_result_not_a_traceback, which asserts the message text verbatim and that the word `Traceback` does not appear.
rulings.B16 — the reader: `_target_tokens`, `_lemmas_for` and `_ending_target` now read the `analysis` G5 writes onto the candidate record; `ResolvedSlot` carries it so a corpus row and an authored row are the same shape to every consumer. The casefolded-surface fallback for authored text is GONE. An authored row that reaches expansion with `analysis: null` stops the stage naming its candidate_id (`MissingAnalysis`) — the coded rule the frozen contract's docstring promises, which no schema keyword can express because a row rejected before the analyser ran legitimately carries null.
rulings.B6 — no locale: `cast.yaml` and `content/es/audio-manifest.json` carry `language: es` + `accent_claim: unverified`; `tts/cast.py` refuses a cast that still declares `locale:` (the FILE, not just the key — an ignored key is a claim nothing enforces); `ACCENT_CLAIMS` has exactly one member and no `verified` one, because the only thing that can produce that claim is the 300-item native-reviewer sample (B3); F2 blocks a manifest carrying `locale`, missing `accent_claim`, or claiming a stronger one; the pack manifest's existing `audio` block carries `accentClaim` (parsePackManifest reads a fixed list of top-level fields and tolerates the rest, so no schema bump and no request to the validators-ci-loader lane was needed); LOCALE_BY_LANGUAGE survives in config/base.py as a URL template variable only, and its docstring now says so.
rulings.B9(b) — lesson 1 is words and fixed phra: An item of `LEXEME_FOCUS_MAX_DISPLAY_TOKENS` (2) display tokens or fewer is a lexeme-focus item and reaches S032/S033/S034 and nothing else (`exercises/shapes.py::focus_for_item`). It is a rule about the ITEM because `route()` cannot catch it: a one-token `word_bank_forward` is a well-formed record of a worthless exercise — one tile among four — and so is a cloze that blanks the only word on screen.

D-S032-NO-ILLUSTRATION.what: S032 `picture_select` is declared in config/g7.py::SHAPES with `available_from: P3` and is therefore UNREACHABLE at P2. `route()` refuses it by name (`ShapeNotAvailable`) rather than the stage quietly not emitting it.
D-S032-NO-ILLUSTRATION.why: `deep/01` §S1: S032's cards are "illustration + target label + tap-to-hear" and the prompt quotes the target word. With no illustration the only thing on a card is the label, one of which is the string the prompt already gave away — the item is answerable by reading the prompt, which is the `answerable by copying` defect the reverse-word-bank fix exists to stop, one rung worse because it is the ANSWER rather than a decoy. Nothing can supply that art or reference it: art/README.md's v1 inventory names the S034 cast avatars and NO per-lexeme illustration, docs/art-and-sound.md's outstanding table lists none, and the frozen `exercise` contract has no field for one — `packbuild/sqlite.py` writes `illustration_ref` from `exercise.get("illustration_ref")`, a key the contract does not define, so every row would ship NULL. The brief's instruction was explicit: a recorded deviation, never a null asset reference.
D-S032-NO-ILLUSTRATION.cost: Three things, all stated rather than absorbed. (1) The NEW WORD pill moves from picture_select to `meaning_select`, which the table already marks `new_word_eligible`; the INV-PACK-50 subset relation (pill-eligible ⊆ lexeme-quoting) is unchanged. (2) `LEXEME_FORM_PLAN` is down to ONE punitive shape, so INV-PACK-07 is no longer discharged by the plan row alone — it is discharged by the row plus `LEXEME_MATCH_SHAPE`, enforced in `_lexeme_pass`: a lexeme is introduced only when a match can also be cut over it, and a lemma that cannot reach both forms is not introduced as a lexeme item at all (it is still taught inside the sentence exercises, which is exactly what already happened to a lemma with no gloss). (3) A RUNTIME cost, which is the one that is easy to discover at P3 instead of here. On origin/main `LEXEME_FORM_PLAN` was `("picture_select", "meaning_select")` and `_lexeme_drafts` emits every plan shape in the lemma's OWN introducing lesson, so a missed lexeme had a SECOND punitive format available inside that lesson. The plan is now one shape and the second form is the match, which D-MATCH-UNIT-SCOPED files in the lesson of its fifth row — a later lesson for every lemma that does not happen to close its own cut. So at P2 a lexeme item has exactly one punitive form inside its introducing lesson (two only for the lemmas a cut's CLOSING row shares a lesson with — `_match_cuts` files each cut under `chunk[-1]`'s lesson, and a lesson introduces one to three lemmas), and a lexeme missed there cannot take EC-MIS-11's preferred branch ("try another eligible authored format") — it takes the fallback ("else replay the original mid-lesson and mark the recycle degraded"). INV-PACK-07 is a PER-ITEM PACK gate counting authored forms anywhere in the pack, so it still passes and is still true; what changed is a runtime recycle branch it cannot see, which is exactly the split EC-MIS-11 calls itself "the runtime twin of EC-MIS-04, whose >=2-authored-forms rule is a build gate that cannot see preference or suspension filtering". ACCEPTED FOR P2: EC-MIS-11 explicitly permits the degraded replay, it never skips the recycle and never ends the session unresolved, and the degradation is per-lesson rather than per-item — the match arrives later in the same unit and restores the preferred branch from then on. It reverts on its own when picture_select returns at P3, since that puts a second in-lesson form back in the plan; no separate P3 work item is needed, but the P3 lane should read this row rather than rediscover the numbers.
D-S032-NO-ILLUSTRATION.reversal: One table cell (`available_from` back to P2) plus the two requests below. Nothing else in the lane depends on the shape being absent.

D-MATCH-UNIT-SCOPED.what: A match's five rows are drawn from the UNIT's eligible lemmas in course order, not the lesson's (`MATCH_LEMMA_SCOPE`), and are filed in the lesson of the fifth row. The final cut of a unit is the unit's LAST FIVE rather than a short tail, so a unit ending with two leftovers re-uses three already-matched lemmas and the leftovers still get a second punitive form.
D-MATCH-UNIT-SCOPED.why: MATCH_PAIRS_PER_EXERCISE is 5 and a real lesson introduces one to three lemmas, so a lesson-scoped match shipped in exactly one place in this repository — the test fixture — and nowhere in a real course. Unit scope is also what `deep/01` §S20 describes (picture-selects, then a 5-pair match, then select-meaning recalls: the match draws on what the learner has met). Without it the INV-PACK-07 construction above is unreachable for almost every lexeme.
D-MATCH-UNIT-SCOPED.cost: A lemma can appear in two matches of its unit, which gives it a third punitive form. A unit with fewer than five eligible lemmas can build no match and therefore introduces no lexeme items; the count is on the runlog (`lexemes_in_a_unit_too_small_to_match`) rather than silent.

D-V5-POS-SETS.what: V5's POS clause compares SETS of attested tags (`validators/exercise.py::pos_sets`, gathered from every banded row and every token G1 tagged in context) and blocks only when the distractor's and the answer's sets are non-empty and disjoint.
D-V5-POS-SETS.why: MEASURED, and it is the defect that stopped the first complete G7 run over the real course: 251 blocking findings, 249 of them this clause, every one of them a distractor the rule core had already drawn from the answer's own POS bucket. `{row["lemma"]: row["pos"]}` keeps one row per lemma (`prima` is a NOUN and a form of `primar`; `frío` is ADJ and NOUN) and a `wrong_form` distractor is an attested SURFACE, so looking it up in a lemma table answers a different question — `viajas` came back PROPN. `DistractorPool` already refuses to decide POS agreement from that map and says so in its docstring; V5 was the last reader that still did.
D-V5-POS-SETS.cost: The clause is weaker for a genuine cross-POS tile whose surface is attested elsewhere as the answer's POS. That is the correct trade: such a tile is not `eliminable without knowing the word`, which is the whole content of the clause.

D-ITEM-KEY-EXCLUSION.what: `_decoys` also excludes everything accepted under the key `validators.exercise.item_keys` will file the record under (`_item_key`), and pass 1 indexes each slot's text, translation AND the token a cloze over it will accept.
D-ITEM-KEY-EXCLUSION.why: An authored sentence has no `source_sentence_id`, so `item_keys` files it under its grammar concept and every authored sentence in that concept is ONE item — while the rule core's exclusion set was per-slot. Over the real course V5 reported `distractor 'hermanos' is an accepted answer of another exercise over the same item` twice. The generator and the validator now agree on what an item is by construction rather than by luck.

D-AUDIO-ID-FUNCTION.what: G7 names a clip with `cast.rebake_key(cast, LESSON_ROLE, text)` — G8's function — instead of `artifacts.sentence_id(lang, text)`, which means G7 now loads `content/<lang>/cast.yaml` and fails by name when it cannot.
D-AUDIO-ID-FUNCTION.why: The module docstring said the two stages used "the same function" and named a different one. Both are 16 hex characters and both are deterministic, so nothing looked wrong until a tree held G7's output AND G8's output at once — which had never happened. Measured over units 1-3 of the real course: G8 baked 284 clips and ALL 198 exercises carrying an `audio_ref` pointed at ids in no `audio` row; G9 refused the pack with `sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. Every listening exercise in the pack would have resolved to no file.
D-AUDIO-ID-FUNCTION.cost: G7 depends on the cast file, which is the honest dependency: a clip id hashes the engine and the voice (INV-AUD-08), so a pack that cannot name its voices cannot carry audio refs. Pinned by `test_inv_aud_08_the_audio_ref_is_the_clip_id_g8_will_actually_bake`, which asserts against `plan_utterances` — G8's own planner — rather than against a second copy of the formula.

D-SPOKEN-TEXT-BY-SHAPE.what: `TARGET_TEXT_FIELD_BY_TYPE` (coarse type -> field) is replaced by `SPOKEN_TEXT_SOURCE` (shape -> where its spoken string comes from) and one function, `stages/g8_bake.py::spoken_text`, that G8 plans from and V7 checks against. `listen_for_the_missing_word` also keeps its gapped sentence as the record's body, per `deep/01` §S038 ("audio plus a sentence with one gap"), and `_gapped` now cuts the blank out of the original text using the analysis offsets so the sentence survives its own punctuation.
D-SPOKEN-TEXT-BY-SHAPE.why: A coarse type is up to four shapes and they do not speak the same string. Three measured consequences: (1) `listen_for_the_missing_word` accepts ONE TOKEN, so the type-keyed rule baked the answer and left the sentence unbaked — the second half of the dangling-foreign-key failure; (2) `speak` and `translate` mapped to `prompt`, which is `instruction\nbody`, so the bank held clips that begin "Speak this sentence"; (3) `translate` and `word_bank` have no audio-bearing shape at all, so every clip baked for them was a clip no exercise plays — bytes inside the 120 MB budget doing nothing and a V7 finding each. The full-course bake was 2,898 clips under the old rule.
D-SPOKEN-TEXT-BY-SHAPE.cost: G8 now decodes the shape from the prompt, so a record whose instruction line no shape renders raises `UnknownShape` instead of being baked on a guess. Test records must carry real prompts; `tests/test_g8_bake.py::_shaped` builds them with `prompt_for`, the renderer G7 uses.

D-EXERCISE-ID-CARRIES-THE-ANSWER.what: `_exercise_id` hashes `(unit, lesson, shape, body, *accepted_answers)` rather than `(unit, lesson, shape, body)`. Every exercise id in the course moves.
D-EXERCISE-ID-CARRIES-THE-ANSWER.why: For a `l1_to_l2` shape the body is the ENGLISH prompt. `Dos más dos es cuatro.` and `Dos más dos son cuatro.` are both slots of unit 2 lesson 12 and both render `Write this in Spanish / Two plus two makes four.`, so they shared one id with two different accepted answers: G9 refused the pack (`UNIQUE constraint failed: exercise.exercise_id`), and downstream of that constraint one FSRS row would have scheduled two items. The accepted answer is exactly what `packbuild.itemid.item_id` already hashes as `preferredSurface`, so the artefact id is now no coarser than the pack id it becomes.
D-EXERCISE-ID-CARRIES-THE-ANSWER.cost: A rebuild moves every exercise id, which is free at P2 (no pack has shipped) and is why INV-PACK-02's additive-only clause is scoped to a major version. The content defect underneath it — two sentences with one translation in one lesson — has no validator: G4/G5's duplicate axis is on the TARGET text only. Filed as a request.

D-PACK-CARRIES-ITS-BANK.what: G9 resolves `baked_clip.path` against G8's stage directory (it is `bank/<clip_id>.opus`, relative to that directory) and FAILS the stage when a declared clip's file is not there; `manifest_violations` additionally refuses a manifest whose measured `audio.bytes` disagrees with the sum of `bytesByPipeline`. The es-mini seed's clip paths are now `bank/…` too, and the replay lays the committed stubs down where a real bake leaves them.
D-PACK-CARRIES-ITS-BANK.why: `_stage_audio_bank` resolved the path against the process's working directory, so `source.exists()` was false for every clip and it copied NOTHING — silently, counting nothing. Measured: a pack whose `audio` table declared 125 clips at `audio/<id>.opus`, whose `audio/` directory was empty, and whose manifest said `audioBytes: 0` — so INV-PACK-15's assertion against the 120 MB budget was being made about zero bytes, and every listening exercise on a device would have taken S151's missing-file path. After the fix the same pack carries 125 files and 580,184 bytes, and the manifest's three audio numbers agree.

D-RTL-ROW-IS-DECIDED.what: The pack's `meta` rows carry `rtl` (a real boolean, `lang in RTL_LANGUAGES`).
D-RTL-ROW-IS-DECIDED.why: V12: "an absent direction flag is not 'false', it is nobody having decided — and the first pack that needs true would ship without it." It blocked every pack this lane built. No v1 language is RTL and INV-I18N-01 pins the app's layout to LTR, so the decision is cheap; not making it was the problem.

measurements.the first complete G7 run over the real: `coursekit build es --only g7 --set align_engine=deterministic` over the committed content (1,584 slots, 1,094 corpus-filled, 490 gaps) exited 0 for the FIRST TIME: `es: 1 stage(s) ok`. Before this lane it stopped at `NotEnoughDistractors: needed 3 distractors for 'tardes' (POS , band unbanded)` (B16). 6,100 exercise records; every P2 shape emitted. shapes = {word_bank_forward 528, word_bank_reverse 352, typed_translate_forward 528, typed_translate_reverse 352, fill_in_the_blank 528, complete_the_translation 352, listen_for_the_missing_word 352, tap_what_you_hear 352, type_what_you_hear 352, complete_the_chat 176, speak_this_sentence 352, read_and_respond 352, listen_and_respond 352, type_the_word_ending 102, meaning_select 882, match_pairs 188}. types_emitted = all seven coarse types the phase can reach. shapes_not_available_in_phase = [picture_select, select_the_character].
measurements.the three G7 gates over that run: INV-PACK-07: 0 blocking. INV-PACK-50: 0 blocking. V5: 0 blocking. The V5 number took four measured rounds and each one is a defect this lane fixed: 251 blocking (249 POS + 2 sibling-accepted) -> 84 (the POS set oracle, D-V5-POS-SETS, and the item-key exclusion, D-ITEM-KEY-EXCLUSION) -> 4 (the shape table declaring which option lists are English) -> 0 (the generator reading the gate's POS oracle for its anchor). Every one of the 251 was a false positive against a distractor the rule core had already drawn from the answer's own POS bucket; none of them was a bad distractor.
measurements.what the lexeme pass did over the real c: 882 lexemes introduced (`meaning_select`), 188 matches cut, 45 lemmas refused for want of a gloss or an option list, 1 lemma in a unit too small to cut a match from. Every introduced lexeme therefore carries meaning_select + at least one match = 2 punitive forms, which is INV-PACK-07 reporting 0 blocking over 6,100 records rather than over a fixture.
measurements.what the alignment bought: alignment_engine=deterministic (the `align` group is not installed on this Mac; the runlog says the quality is `unmeasured` and that such a pack must not ship), alignment_pairs_written=1,578, word_bank_hints=721, ending_drills_planned=176, ending_drills_written=102. The 102 is new: an authored sentence now carries an analysis, so it gets its ending drills like any other — before B16's read side it could not.
measurements.phrase slots over the real course: ZERO,: `phrase_slots=0`. Two reasons, both outside this lane's files and both named in the requests above. (1) `config/g5.py::MIN_TOKENS` is 3, so no short item survives G5 at all; the live run applied ruling B9(b) as a RUNTIME override for lesson 1 only. (2) Even then, `stages/g7_expand.py::_load` keeps the LAST accepted candidate per slot (`candidates[key] = row`), and G6 leaves 6,110 of 9,867 candidates accepted — several per slot — so which survivor ships is whichever G5 wrote last. The lesson-1 diagnostic shard lists its one- and two-token strings first, so the four-token ones won. Deterministic but not a stated rule; recorded rather than changed, because changing it changes which sentence ships in every gap slot of the course and that is a content decision, not a G7 one. The phrase path is therefore covered by three tests (including a real stage run through the CLI) and NOT by the live run.
measurements.the audio bake is a three-hour job, whic: G8 must bake 2,898 distinct clips for this course (6,100 exercise records deduplicated by re-bake key, plus the four cast samples). Measured on this Mac: ~15 clips/minute through synthesise -> master -> encode -> decode -> measure -> re-encode, i.e. about three hours for the bank. `.github/workflows/pack-ci.yml` gives `build-es` 90 minutes. The bake is not slow by accident — INV-AUD-08 measures loudness on the DECODED shipped file and re-encodes until it lands inside half the tolerance — so the fix is not a faster loop; it is a bigger budget, a cached bank keyed on the re-bake key, or a bake job of its own (which is what B2 deleted for a different reason).
measurements.the defect chain the live run walked, in: Each fix uncovered the next gate, and every one of them was invisible until a tree held both G7's and G8's output: (1) B16's reader — G7 stopped at `NotEnoughDistractors` for 'tardes'; (2) V5 251 -> 84 -> 4 -> 0 blocking over four fixes; (3) `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` — G7 and G8 named the same clip with different functions, 198 of 198 audio refs dangling; (4) `UNIQUE constraint failed: exercise.exercise_id` — two sentences with one English translation in unit 2 lesson 12; (5) `UNIQUE constraint failed: exercise_item_tag.…` — a repeated lemma in one sentence's tag list; (6) a pack that declared 125 clips, carried none, and reported `audioBytes: 0`; (7) V12's absent `rtl` row. G9's three gates caught (3)-(6) only because it finally ran.
measurements.the fixture regenerated twice, and what: `packages/core/src/packs/__fixtures__/es-mini` was rebuilt from the real G9 after each manifest-shape change and the diff reviewed as source: first `audio.accentClaim: "unverified"` (plus `builtAt`), then the `rtl` meta row (which moves `payloadSha256` and the sqlite bytes, not a single item id — INV-PACK-41 in action). `seed.json`'s three clip paths moved from `audio/…` to `bank/…`, which is what a real bake writes.

contractGapsFiledAsRequests: `coursekit/artifacts.py::EXERCISE` has no field for an ILLUSTRATION. `packbuild/sqlite.py` writes the pack's `illustration_ref` column from `exercise.get("illustration_ref")` — a key the frozen contract does not define — so the column is NULL for every row of every pack, and S032 cannot ship (D-S032-NO-ILLUSTRATION). REQUEST to the deps/contract lane: add `illustration_ref: string | null` to the EXERCISE record, which moves contract_digest(). REQUEST to the art track: per-lexeme illustrations readable at the card sizes `deep/08` §10 names; art/README.md's v1 inventory does not list them today.

The same record still has no `shape` field and no field for the NEW WORD pill — p2-g7.json's standing requests, unchanged. This lane adds one consequence: with the pill's shape changing from picture_select to meaning_select, the only record-level evidence that the pill clause of INV-PACK-50 holds is still the structural subset relation asserted by `shapes.assert_pill_shapes_quote_lexemes`.

An AUTHORED exercise has no per-item id on the frozen record: `source_sentence_id` is null and nothing carries the candidate_id, so `item_keys` can only file it under its grammar concept. That is right for INV-PACK-07 (the grammar drills need the concept key or each becomes a single-form item) and wrong for V5's cross-exercise clause, which then treats thirty authored sentences as one item. D-ITEM-KEY-EXCLUSION makes the generator agree with that reading; the better fix is a `source_item_id` on the EXERCISE record, which is the deps lane's file.

`config/g5.py::MIN_TOKENS` is 3, so no one- or two-token item can reach G7 from a real build today: the committed lesson-1 candidates (`Hola, hola.`, `Bueno, hola.`) are rejected on the `length` axis and u1/l1's nine slots starve. Ruling B9(b) puts a per-lesson MIN_TOKENS of 1 in G5's lane. G7's half of that ruling is implemented and unit-tested here; over the real tree it was exercised by a RUNTIME override in the live-run driver (not committed), because config/g5.py is not this lane's file.

`config/g5.py`'s over-generation floor is 20 authored candidates per slot, and the lesson-1 window admits about eleven in-vocabulary strings in total (B9). Even with B9(b) applied, u1/l1 fails the floor before any of this lane's code runs. Either the floor is per-lesson too, or lesson 1 is authored against a wider window (B9(a), the lemma-normalisation table).

liveRun.what ran: G7 over the WHOLE committed Spanish course, then G8 and G9 over units 1-3 of it, then `coursekit validate es`. Build root and content root were scratch copies (`COURSEKIT_BUILD_ROOT`/`COURSEKIT_CONTENT_ROOT`); the g0-g2 artefacts are the committed tree's, g3 and g4 were re-run because the checked-in `build/` tree was a STALE G4 (920 gaps at gap_fraction 0.58, from a curriculum before the ledger freeze) and the current one is 1,584 slots / 1,094 filled / 490 gaps / gap_fraction 0.3093 / 0 cross-unit repeats, digest-identical to the committed gap brief.
liveRun.the two diagnostic deviations, named: (1) u1/l1's nine slots were filled from an UNCOMMITTED diagnostic shard (author string `DIAGNOSTIC ONLY - not committed content`), 20 candidates per slot, generated from the gap brief's own windows; the committed lesson-1 rows were removed from the scratch copies to avoid G5's cross-file collision guard. (2) ruling B9(b)'s per-lesson `MIN_TOKENS = 1` was applied as a RUNTIME override for lesson 1 only, because `config/g5.py` is another lane's file.
